This workdir has a small CSV-like record codec: dsv.py turns a list of string fields into one delimited line and back, and table.py reads/writes whole tables on top of it. Encoding and decoding are supposed to be exact inverses. Encoding is fine -- a value like he said "hi" is correctly written out with the quote doubled and the field wrapped in quotes (see README.md and the passing tests in test_dsv.py). The problem is DECODING: any field that contains a quote comes back wrong. For example, decoding the line that the encoder produces for ['he said "hi"', 'plain'] returns the field truncated at the first quote instead of the original text, so table.loads(table.dumps(rows)) no longer equals rows whenever a value has a quote in it. Fix the decoder so round-trip works again for fields with embedded quotes. Keep encoding working exactly as it does now -- don't change the quoting convention or break the existing encode tests; fix the real cause in the library rather than editing the tests.
